  "from here through the Call to Action."
- CR-2 (faq:scaling still asserted unbuilt Bridge mitigations as
  present fact, contradicting the same fix already applied to
  faq:tech-risks 40 lines earlier): fixed, converted to explicit
  built-vs-design voice, cross-referenced to the Feature Appendix.

  "signing already uses an isolated GNUPGHOME", is false): verified
  against internal/pgp/sign.go directly -- Sign() has no --homedir,
  uses the ambient system keyring; only Verify() isolates. The same
  false claim existed in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's Design Invariants
  section (the likely source of the error) and is corrected there too.
- CR-4 (kill-switch dates): the reviewer's proposed correction
  (v0.14.0/2026-04-13 as "the first release with binaries") is ITSELF
  wrong -- verified directly via `gh api`: v0.1.0 (2026-03-13) already
  shipped all 4 platform binaries + checksums, and there are 29
  releases total, not the 9 the reviewer's query returned. Original
  dates were correct and are kept. The real half of CR-4 -- the
  document names a decision but never makes one -- is fixed: added an
  explicit recommendation not to run the kill switch as written, and
  to re-baseline it to the Must Do items' own one-quarter accountability
  window instead.

Also fixed, each independently verified: W-2/W-9 (two risk-table cells
left self-contradicting fragments from the pre-fix wording), W-6

estimate" self-description per an original-round finding), W-7

already softened to "recommended"), W-11 (one straight-quote pair
breaking LaTeX's quote convention), W-13 (added an explicit note that
the Feature Appendix's 5-category split, versus the template's 3, is
deliberate -- it's the document's core honesty mechanism, not an
oversight). W-8 (reviewer claimed "five releases" should be "six") and
part of CR-4 were checked and found already correct -- v0.16.3 was
never tagged, so five is the accurate count; not changed.

Remaining warnings from this round (W-1 worker-sandbox terminology,

none block shippability per the reviewer's own priority ordering,
which named items 1-4 (all now fixed) as the PASS threshold.
EOF
)"
